SMWMFL

The National Weather Service in Miami has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Biscayne Bay...
Coastal waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL out 20 NM...
Waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL from 20 to 60 NM
excluding the territorial waters of Bahamas...

waterspouts was located 15 nm east of Port Everglades, or 16 nm
northeast of Sunny Isles, moving southeast at 15 knots.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Virginia Key, Miami Beach, Bal Harbour, Surfside, Indian Creek, Bay
Harbor Islands, and North Bay Village.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches; Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast; Santa Barbara County Southeastern Coast
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Dangerous and potentially life threatening rip currents
and breaking waves due to elevated surf expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches, Santa Barbara County
Central Coast Beaches, Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast
and Santa Barbara County Southeastern Coast.

* WHEN...Through Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents will be widespread and very strong, potentially
pulling swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can wash people
off beaches and rocks. Pooling of sea water is possible around
high tide at beach areas that is uncommon with normal tidal
ranges. Enhanced beach erosion is also possible. No
significant damage is expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides will occur around 6.5 feet at
730pm today and 6.5 feet at 830pm on Tuesday.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands; Ventura County Beaches; Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal
flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 5 to 8 feet with local sets to 12 feet and dangerous
and potentially life threatening rip currents, largest on
south- facing shores.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands, Ventura County
Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...Until 11 PM PDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents will be widespread and very strong, potentially pulling
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause
injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small
boats near shore. Significant beach erosion will occur. Flooding
of sea water is likely, around the time of high tide, over
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas such as parking lots,
beaches, walkways, and low-lying roads. Of particular concern
will be the Alamitos Peninsula area in Long Beach where coastal
flooding will potentially cause local damage to structures near
time of high tides. Other areas that will be susceptible to
coastal flooding during the next couple of days include Catalina
Island, and Oxnard to Malibu (including Point Mugu).

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides will occur around 7 feet at 7pm today
and 7.2 feet at 8pm on Tuesday.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Elevated water levels expected. Water levels could rise
1 to 2 feet above the normal high tide line along the Yukon
Delta Coast, and 3 to 5 feet above the normal high tide line in
the Eastern Norton Sound.

* WHERE...Yukon Delta Coast and Eastern Norton Sound.

* WHEN...Wednesday September 9 through Friday September 11.

* IMPACTS...Localized beach erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Southwest winds will steadily ramp up
Wednesday into Thursday, remaining elevated through Friday,
before gradually subsiding Friday night into Saturday. Winds
will peak Thursday and Friday, with gusts around 40 to 50 mph
expected.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
FFWHFO

The National Weather Service in Honolulu has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The island of Kauai in Kauai County

* Until 200 PM HST.

* At 1111 AM HST, significant rises in water level have occurred
along the South Fork of the Wailua River over the past hour due to
heavy rain upstream. While heavy rain is diminishing, additional
runoff is likely and could lead to flooding issues farther
downstream near the river mouth in Wailua. This warning replaces
the warning previously in effect for the north central portion of
Kauai including the Hanalei area.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rain.

SOURCE...Gauges reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Lihue, Kapaa, Princeville, Kilauea, North Fork Wailua Trails,
Wailua Homesteads, Hanalei, Wailua, Moloaa, Wainiha, Anahola and
Alakai Swamp Trails.
